newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine seeks $900 mn from World Bank in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine seeks $900 mn from World Bank in 1997.

text.p: Ukraine expects to receive $900 million in World Bank credits next year for energy and agriculture development projects, deputy prime minister Viktor Pynzenyk said late on Tuesday.

"The possible funding from the World Bank would be greater than ever before," Pynzenyk said at a news conference following a Washington visit to attend talks with the bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
He said Ukraine requires increased funding to further its economic reform programme, started in 1994 by President Leonid Kuchma.
"In this regard we were talking in high figures, and the total amount of credits could exceed $900 million," he said.
The World Bank is due to give Ukraine $550 million in credits this year. In 1994-95 it provided $527 million.

An IMF mission is due to visit Kiev later this month to continue talks on Ukraine's request for a $2.5-3 billion, three-year Extended Fund Facility (EFF) to succeed the $864 million stand-by programme agreed in May and set to expire early next year.

World Bank credits would fund large projects such as energy sector reform, export guarantees for the agriculture sector, and restructuring Ukraine's ageing and inefficient coal sector, said Pynzenyk. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
